report.summary: Chunk 6 of vendors.py: defines assemble(), ask(), _reply(), _dispatch(), and _CliAdapter class. assemble() builds prompt text with egress withholding; ask() orchestrates floor check, token ceiling, dispatch, and error handling; _reply() constructs VendorReply; _dispatch() is abstract; _CliAdapter() initializes with profile and lane.
risks: assemble | medium | WITHHELD BY EGRESS LANE message is always added when blocked non-empty; may leak that paths exist. | Check if presence of withheld paths is acceptable information disclosure.

ask | medium | Exception catch-all may mask specific errors; stderr includes exception type and message which could leak internals. | Ensure exceptions are logged appropriately and stderr is sanitized.
_CliAdapter.__init__ | low | Uses COUNCIL_PROFILES global; assumes it is already populated. | Verify import order and initialization of COUNCIL_PROFILES.

handoff.purpose: Defines assemble(), ask(), _reply(), _dispatch(), and _CliAdapter class for vendor adapters.

symbols.name: assemble
symbols.note: Instance method of CouncilAdapter; builds prompt text with role, evidence, and withheld paths.

symbols.name: ask
symbols.note: Instance method of CouncilAdapter; orchestrates floor check, token ceiling check, dispatch, and error handling.

symbols.name: _reply
symbols.note: Instance method of CouncilAdapter; constructs VendorReply with vendor metadata.

symbols.name: _dispatch
symbols.note: Instance method of CouncilAdapter; abstract method to be implemented by subclasses.

symbols.name: _CliAdapter
symbols.note: Subclass of CouncilAdapter for CLI vendors; initializes profile from COUNCIL_PROFILES.

claims.why: The comment says 'their contents are never rendered' but the method actually renders the contents of withheld paths in the WITHHELD BY EGRESS LANE section, listing the paths themselves.

claims.text: The runner must not be reachable from a refused call.
claims.why: The code returns early with a refusal reply before any dispatch or runner invocation.

claims.text: The secret never leaves the process, and the recorded reason names the rule, never the bytes.
claims.why: The refusal reply includes only the rule name (refusal.rule) and does not include the prompt or any secret data.

claims.text: Charged BEFORE dispatch from the assembled prompt: a per-call timeout does not bound token spend, and reconciling after the call is not a budget.
claims.why: The token count check occurs before _dispatch is called, ensuring the prompt is not sent if over the ceiling.

claims.text: A vendor must never take the council down
claims.why: The dispatch call is wrapped in a try-except that catches all exceptions and returns an error VendorReply.

observations.what: assemble method includes a comment 'their contents are never rendered' but the method actually renders the list of withheld paths in the output.
ask method catches all Exception types, which may hide programming errors or system-level exceptions.
_CliAdapter.__init__ references COUNCIL_PROFILES without checking if it is defined or populated; assumes global state.
